title: Changing a portion re-rounds every figure to one decimal each time, so label figures drift and salt is lost
where: Change sheet on Today and past days; web/lib/mm/user-data.ts:55-61 (withPortion), web/lib/mm/stores.ts:174-176 (setLogPortion)
evidence: In the browser, Porridge was logged as {calories 369, protein 11.2, salt 0.07, sugar 0.3}. After Change → ½ portion → 1 portion it is stored as {calories 369, protein 11.2, salt 0, sugar 0.4} (walk2 output, localStorage mm.v1.log). Replaying withPortion on {protein 7.3, carbs 31.7, fat 9.9} gives 7.4 / 31.8 / 10 after ½ then 1, and 7.2 / 31.6 / 9.8 after 3 → ½ → 1. The figure is scaled from the already-rounded current value every time (CLAUDE.md rule 1: figures come only from the label). Halves also give 184.5 kcal entries, so two rows each read "185 kcal" while their meal header reads "369 kcal". tests/logPortion.test.ts only checks values that divide cleanly.
fix: Keep the as-logged figures. The first time the portion changes, store a `logged: Nutrients` (one portion) on the entry and accept it in sanitizeLog. withPortion then always scales from `logged`: calories rounded to whole kcal, grams to 0.1, salt to 0.01. Going back to 1 restores `logged` exactly and drops `portion`. Add a test for ½ → 1 and 3 → ½ → 1 with salt 0.07 and protein 7.3.

title: There is no way to add a forgotten food to a past day, or to fix a wrong typed number on one

Stamp the entry at that day's time for the meal (breakfast 08:00, lunch 13:00, dinner 19:00, snacks 15:00 local) and set `meal`. Remove the stale "read-only" comment. Entries older than the 2-day sync window simply stay on the device, as past entries already do.

title: Supermarket products are logged with Open Food Facts numbers that contradict the shop label the app already holds
where: Add food › Choose a supermarket product (and its How much step); web/app/app/_components/addfood/ProductPick.tsx:30
evidence: ProductPick calls useGroceryCatalogue(null), which loads the old catalogue in public/groceries/*.json (19,144 products; only 32 carry source:'retailer', all the rest are community numbers). It never uses the shops' own lists with labels in public/groceries/all/*.json (Sainsbury's 13,933 labelled, Morrisons 12,582, Waitrose 8,239), which Groceries and Recipes use. Walk (17-product-results.png, 19-howmuch-40.png): 'Scott's Porage Original Porridge Oats 1kg · Sainsbury's · 272 kcal · 13g protein per 100 g'. For the same barcode 5000108022176, all/sainsburys.json holds the label 374 kcal, 11 g protein, 60 g carbs (same:waitrose); the catalogue says 24 g carbs, which is impossible for oats. 40 g logs as 109 kcal instead of 150. Every product tried in the walk said 'From Open Food Facts contributors (community data) ... Check the pack.', and the list row names 'Sainsbury's' with no hint that the figures are community data. Most of a shop's range (for example nearly all of Waitrose) can't be found here at all.

Log ShopNutrition per 100 through amountNutrients and say where the figures come from exactly as the shop item page does: label, 'same product at {shop}' (sameAs), community (community:true) or the UK government figures (govFood). Fall back to the OFF catalogue only for a typed or scanned barcode that no shop list holds, and keep the community wording there. Add a vitest that a product with both records logs the shop label's figures.

title: Changing a portion re-rounds and saves the figures, so published numbers drift and rows stop adding up
where: Today › Change › How much did you have?; web/lib/mm/user-data.ts:55 (withPortion), web/lib/mm/stores.ts setLogPortion
evidence: withPortion scales the saved figures by new/old and rounds every one to 1 decimal place. Live walk on Today with a Five Guys Hamburger (salt 1.14 g): ½ portion, then 1 portion, saved salt 1.2 (log dump in walk 3). Scratch vitest (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-amanmarwaha-MenuAi/2d77750c-825b-4557-9812-d2804c28296a/scratchpad/audit/add-food/probe/probe.test.ts): {calories 523, protein 12.3, carbs 61.7, fat 8.5, salt 0.35, sugar 4.25} goes ½ and back to protein 12.4, carbs 61.8, fat 8.6, salt 0.4, sugar 4.2. Calories become fractional (261.5, 784.5). Each row shows 262 kcal but the meal and dial total 523, so two halves read 262 + 262 = 524 against a total of 523. CLAUDE.md rule 1: the restaurant's figures are changed, and salt loses its second decimal.
fix: Keep the logged portion's own figures on the entry. On the first change add perPortion: Nutrients (the original snapshot) and always compute nutrients = round(perPortion × portion): calories whole (halfUp), grams to 1 decimal place, salt to 2 (as amountNutrients does). Portion 1 then returns the exact original. Sanitize perPortion in sanitizeLog (the same check as nutrients) and keep it through sync. Extend tests/logPortion.test.ts: a ½ → 1 round trip gives back the original object, and calories are always whole.

title: Wording and number formatting differ between screens
where: web/app/app/eat-out/favourites/page.tsx:49,59,71; web/app/app/search/page.tsx:126,164; web/app/app/eat-out/page.tsx:95; web/app/app/_components/ChainRow.tsx:34; web/app/app/chain/ChainScreen.tsx:230
evidence:
- The restaurant page's star button says "Favourite". My favourite restaurants uses "Save/Saved" with a star, and on the dish page "Save" with a heart means My meals (26-favourites.png, 14-dish-allergens.png).
- Search headings say "Chains" and "Items" while every other screen says restaurants and dishes.
- The "Near me" line ends with a full stop and its neighbours don't.
- Item counts have no thousands separator ("1218 items", Domino's "1349 items") while calories use "1,415 kcal".
- The favourites search's visible placeholder is "Type a restaurant's name" but its accessible name is "Search restaurants".
- Pip decorates the favourites empty state, though the 20 Nov Pip audit took him off Search's.
fix:
- Use "Favourite/Favourited" with the star on My favourite restaurants.
- Rename the search headings "Restaurants" and "Dishes" (this is SPEC §7.3 copy, so ask the founder first).
- Drop the stray full stop.
- Format counts with toLocaleString("en-GB") in ChainRow and the restaurant header.
- Make the aria-label match the placeholder.
- Use a plain icon in the favourites empty state.
